T: Snow's late in Vermont. Dinner isn't.
D: Two army mates turned song-and-dance stars put on a show to save their old general's struggling Vermont inn.
P: Serve the snacks when the show at the Columbia Inn begins.
S: Midnight liverwurst on rye and buttermilk
Liverwurst, mustard, pickles and red onion on rye, with cold buttermilk

Rye sandwiches of smooth liverwurst with mustard, pickles and red onion, cut into fingers and served with little glasses of cold buttermilk. Spread 8 slices of rye bread with 30g soft butter and a thin layer of wholegrain mustard. Slice 250g liverwurst or smooth pork pâté and lay it over 4 of the slices. Top with thinly sliced dill pickles and a few rings of red onion, then the other slices of bread. Press down, trim the crusts and cut each sandwich into 4 fingers. Pour 400ml well-chilled buttermilk into 4 small glasses and serve together.
Light choux puffs baked with sharp cheddar
Warm cheddar choux puffs straight from the oven, the kind of welcome snack a country lodge puts out for guests.
M: Roast turkey breast with stuffing, cranberry sauce and roast potatoes
Roast turkey breast with sage stuffing, cranberry sauce and crisp roast potatoes, a proper country inn Christmas dinner.
W: Coconut cake layers with cream cheese frosting rolled in coconut
White coconut layer cake covered in cream cheese icing and coconut like fresh snow on Christmas Eve.
K: Chilled egg custard drink with nutmeg, brandy on the side
Spiced eggnog with nutmeg, with brandy on the side for the adults.

dishes.n: Midnight liverwurst on rye and buttermilk
dishes.make_ahead: Make the sandwiches up to 2 hours ahead, covered with a damp cloth in the fridge; pour the buttermilk to serve

steps.text: Spread the bread with butter and a thin layer of mustard.
Slice the liverwurst and lay it over half the slices. Top with pickles and red onion, then the other slices.
Press down, trim the crusts and cut into fingers.
Pour the buttermilk into small glasses and serve together.

veg.n: Midnight mushroom pate on rye and buttermilk
veg.make_ahead: Make the mushroom pate up to 2 days ahead in the fridge; build the sandwiches up to 2 hours ahead

steps.text: Fry the mushrooms, garlic and thyme in a third of the butter until dark and dry.
Blitz with the cream cheese, salt and pepper until smooth, then cool.
Spread the bread with the rest of the butter and a thin layer of mustard.
Spread the mushroom pate thickly over half the slices. Top with pickles and red onion, then the other slices.
Press down, trim the crusts and cut into fingers.
Pour the buttermilk into small glasses and serve together.

dishes.make_ahead: Make the choux paste up to 1 day ahead, covered in the fridge; pipe and bake on the night, best warm

steps.text: Bring water and the butter to the boil, beat in the flour until it forms a ball, then cool.
Beat in the eggs one at a time, then the cheddar.
Pipe small balls onto lined trays.
Bake at 200C until puffed and golden.

dishes.make_ahead: Mix the stuffing up to 1 day ahead in the fridge; rub the turkey with butter and herbs up to 1 day ahead

steps.text: Rub the turkey with some of the butter and the herbs.
Roast at 180C.
Mix the breadcrumbs with the onion, chopped sage and melted butter and bake the stuffing alongside the turkey.
Toss the potatoes in oil and roast on another tray.
Rest the turkey and serve with stuffing, cranberry sauce and potatoes.

veg.make_ahead: Mix the stuffing up to 1 day ahead in the fridge; rub the celeriac with butter and herbs up to 1 day ahead

steps.text: Scrub the celeriac, trim the root and rub with 20g of the butter, softened, and the herbs.
Wrap loosely in foil and roast at 180C, then unwrap for the last 20 minutes until golden and tender to a skewer.
Mix the breadcrumbs with the onion, chopped sage and the remaining butter, melted, and bake the stuffing alongside for the last 25 minutes.
Toss the potatoes in the oil and roast on another tray.
Rest the celeriac for 10 minutes, cut into wedges and serve with the stuffing, cranberry sauce and potatoes.

dishes.make_ahead: Bake and wrap the cakes up to 2 days ahead; ice and roll in coconut on the day

steps.text: Beat the butter with the sugar until pale, then add the eggs, flour, some of the coconut and the coconut milk.
Bake in two tins at 175C.
Cool the cakes.
Beat the cream cheese with the icing sugar, sandwich and cover the cakes.
Roll the sides in the rest of the coconut.
Whisk the yolks with the sugar.
Heat the milk, cream and cinnamon stick until steaming, whisk into the yolks and return to the pan.
Stir over low heat until it coats a spoon.
Chill.
Serve with grated nutmeg and brandy on the side.
Whisk the yolks with the sugar.
Heat the milk, cream, cinnamon stick and vanilla until steaming, whisk into the yolks and return to the pan.
Stir over low heat until it coats a spoon.
Chill.
Serve with grated nutmeg.

s.n: Midnight liverwurst on rye and buttermilk
s.note: Liverwurst, mustard, pickles and red onion on rye, with cold buttermilk
s.how: Spread 8 slices of rye bread with 30g soft butter and a thin layer of wholegrain mustard. Slice 250g liverwurst or smooth pork pâté and lay it over 4 of the slices. Top with thinly sliced dill pickles and a few rings of red onion, then the other slices of bread. Press down, trim the crusts and cut each sandwich into 4 fingers. Pour 400ml well-chilled buttermilk into 4 small glasses and serve together.

s.note: Light choux puffs baked with sharp cheddar
s.how: Bring 250ml water and 100g butter to the boil, beat in 150g plain flour until it forms a ball, then cool. Beat in 4 eggs one at a time and 120g grated cheddar. Pipe small balls and bake at 200C for 25 minutes.

m.note: Roast turkey breast with stuffing, cranberry sauce and roast potatoes
m.how: Rub a 1.5kg turkey breast with butter and herbs and roast at 180C for 1 hour 20 minutes. Bake stuffing made from 150g breadcrumbs, a diced onion, chopped sage and melted butter. Serve with cranberry sauce and 1kg roast potatoes.

w.note: Coconut cake layers with cream cheese frosting rolled in coconut
w.how: Beat 200g butter and 200g sugar, add 4 eggs, then 250g self-raising flour, 60g coconut and 150ml coconut milk. Bake in two tins at 175C for 28 minutes. Cover with 250g cream cheese beaten with 200g icing sugar and roll in the rest of the coconut.

d.note: Chilled egg custard drink with nutmeg, brandy on the side
d.how: Whisk 4 egg yolks with 100g sugar. Heat 600ml milk, 200ml cream and a cinnamon stick until steaming, whisk into the yolks and stir over low heat until it coats a spoon. Chill and serve with grated nutmeg and brandy on the side.
